mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has deteriorated in three of the last four weeks (-20.1, -18.3, -21.1, -24.4), so the four-week level entering the next 28 days is above the current run-rate; the persistence of this downward momentum drags the next 28-day mean below the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -21.1 (t-1w) to -24.4 (t-0w), the lowest value in the four-week window
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to -20.98 (the last-28-day mean), rejecting the momentum-continuation claim.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing from positive to negative (0.7 to -2.7) marks the end of the replenishment phase and the onset of broad trip suppression; households cut all non-essential outings in the same week, so RETAIL_REC falls further within one week of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0.0 percent change for the first time in the four-week window
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM went from +0.7 at t-1w to -2.7 at t-0w, its first negative print in the window
failure_condition: In weeks where GROCERY_PHARM crosses below zero, the following 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the crossing-week RETAIL_REC value.

mechanism_narrative: Commuting collapse is joint: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both set new four-week lows in the same week (-26.3 and -27.1). Because retail-and-recreation footfall is dominated by trip-chaining around commutes, the co-movement of both series predicts a joint drag on RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks that exceeds the sum of either channel alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reached their four-week minimum at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days whenever TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline together for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has fallen from 12.4 to 1.9, meaning the mid-summer outdoor substitute for indoor leisure is exhausting its seasonal peak. As the outdoor alternative loses its draw, a share of discretionary trips rotates back into indoor retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from 12.4 at t-2w to 4.0 at t-1w to 1.9 at t-0w
regime_hint: post-peak summer seasonal lull with no new restrictions
failure_condition: Following two consecutive weekly PARKS declines of more than 2 points, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES sliding monotonically (-21.7, -23.7, -26.4, -27.1) while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline is the signature of newly imposed capacity limits rather than voluntary caution; mandated capacity caps bind directly on retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC keeps falling for the full four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -25.0 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +1.0
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined every week while RESIDENTIAL held at +1.3, non-negative throughout
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or above the last 28-day mean in periods where WORKPLACES is below -25 and RESIDENTIAL is above +1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT leads RETAIL_REC by roughly one week in this snapshot, and TRANSIT printed its steepest weekly drop of the window (-23.3 to -26.3) at t-0w. Because transit ridership is the earliest observable behavioural commitment to an outing, the transit plunge forecasts a further RETAIL_REC decline within the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2.0 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 3.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: In the week following a TRANSIT drop of more than 2.0 points, the 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC rises above the prior week's RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w level of RETAIL_REC (-24.4) is 3.3 points below the four-week average, so the last-28-day mean is inflated relative to the current state. If the current level persists even without further deterioration, the next 28-day mean mechanically prints below the trailing mean, giving a negative direction on pure carry-over arithmetic.
evidence_refs: fact:last-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is -20.98 versus a t-0w reading of -24.4
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds -20.98 while RETAIL_REC stays at or below -24.0 in every intervening week.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w readings across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES and PARKS all hit four-week lows in the same week, a one-week joint shock consistent with a single transient event rather than a new trend. Households treat it as temporary, so discretionary trips rebound and RETAIL_REC recovers over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT and PARKS all set a four-week low in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:all three series reached their four-week minimum at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with no new binding restrictions announced
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline in each of the two weeks following the joint four-week-low week, leaving the 14-day mean below the pre-shock 14-day mean.
